title: Eye Roll Emoji 🙄 Meaning: Sarcasm, Annoyance, “Ugh”
description: 🙄 is an eye roll: “ugh,” “obviously,” or “here we go again.” Learn when it is playful, when it is contemptuous, and why it stings more than you may intend.
summary: 🙄 shows a face with its eyes rolled upward. It expresses exasperation, sarcasm or disdain: the sender finds something annoying, obvious, ridiculous or tiresome. It can be affectionate teasing between friends or a sharp dismissal, depending on who it is aimed at.
meaning: An eye roll in person needs no translation, and the emoji keeps the meaning intact. 🙄 says “oh, please.” It answers boasts, excuses, repeated complaints, and anything the sender has heard too many times. The feeling combines boredom and irritation with a judgment attached: whatever prompted it does not deserve to be taken seriously.

It is one of the main ways to mark sarcasm in text. “Because that worked so well last time 🙄” would be ambiguous without the face. With it, the reader hears the tone of voice. People also attach it to their own statements to signal reluctance, as in “fine, I'll go 🙄,” where it means agreement under protest.

A lot of everyday use is self-directed or situational, and harmless. “Forgot my password again 🙄” rolls the eyes at one's own habits. “Rain on the one day I washed the car 🙄” rolls them at life. Used like this, the emoji is a small release of frustration and nobody is being insulted.

Pointed at a person, it has real bite. Rolling your eyes at someone says their words are not worth a response, and relationship researchers and etiquette writers alike treat the gesture as a sign of contempt. In arguments, a 🙄 often does more damage than an angry reply would. Friends and couples use it playfully all the time, but it depends on both sides knowing it is a joke.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It labels sarcasm, groans at bad jokes and shows reluctant agreement. Friends send it when someone humble-brags or states the obvious. In a tense exchange, though, it reads as “you're being ridiculous,” and the recipient will likely respond to the disrespect more than to anything else you wrote.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Flirty banter is full of 🙄. A reply like “you're so full of yourself 🙄” pretends to be unimpressed while clearly enjoying the conversation. The clue is that they keep talking and teasing. If the eye roll comes with short answers and no humor, it is real annoyance and a sign to ease off.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It is a stock reaction to bad takes, predictable outrage, and corporate statements nobody believes. Quote posts use it to dismiss an opinion without rebutting it. It is common in complaints about relatable nuisances, from slow walkers to subscription pop-ups, where the audience is expected to roll their eyes along.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Use it only about shared, impersonal annoyances with colleagues you trust, such as a meeting invite landing at 4:55 on a Friday. Never direct it at a person's message, a customer, or a manager's decision in a public channel. Screenshots travel, and an eye roll is hard to explain as anything except disrespect.

examples.text: He's “too busy” to text but posted six stories 🙄
examples.meaning: Not believing an excuse and annoyed by it.

examples.text: Yes Mom, I'm wearing a jacket 🙄
examples.meaning: Mild exasperation at being fussed over.
Sarcasm about a minor recurring irritation.
Conceding a point grudgingly and playfully.

examples.text: “I don't even try and I get A's” 🙄
examples.meaning: Quoting someone's humble-brag to mock it.

examples.text: Left my coffee on the roof of the car. Again 🙄
examples.meaning: Frustration aimed at the sender's own forgetfulness.

combos.meaning: Extreme exasperation; the sender can hardly believe how tiresome this is.
Something is ridiculous but funny; the eye roll is good-natured.
“Stop, I can't with this,” refusing to hear more.

confusedWith.difference: 😒 glances sideways and stays annoyed, often with hurt or jealousy behind it. 🙄 looks up and dismisses. The side-eye says “I'm upset with you”; the eye roll says “this is beneath my attention.”

On some older designs the upward gaze of 🙄 made it look thoughtful, and the two were occasionally mixed up. 🤔 has a hand on its chin and means pondering or doubt. 🙄 has no hand and means exasperation.

🙃 signals irony through a strained smile turned on its head, usually about the sender's own bad luck. 🙄 is more direct and can target other people. 🙃 is “this is fine, apparently”; 🙄 is “give me a break.”

avoid: Do not send it during a serious argument, because it communicates contempt and makes resolution harder.
Avoid it in reply to someone's worry or complaint that matters to them, even if it seems minor to you.
Keep it out of messages to customers, teachers, managers or anyone who could reasonably read it as insolence.
design: A yellow face with large white eyes whose pupils are rolled to the top, usually paired with a small flat or slightly frowning mouth. Current designs from the major vendors are closely matched. Some earlier versions looked less irritated, with a mouth closer to a slight smile, which made the emoji read as coy or pensive to some users before the designs converged.

faqs.a: It can be. Rolling your eyes at a person dismisses what they said. Between friends who tease each other, or about a situation instead of a person, it is fine. In conflicts and formal settings it is among the most provocative smileys you can send.

faqs.q: What does 🙄 mean from a girl or a guy?
faqs.a: Either playful exasperation or real annoyance. If the chat is light and they keep engaging, they are teasing you. If it comes after you repeated yourself, made an excuse or bragged, they are fed up. Tone before and after is the guide.
Very often. It is commonly added to a sentence to show the opposite is meant, such as “love that for me 🙄.” It also expresses straightforward irritation with no sarcasm, as in “ugh, traffic 🙄.”

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🙄 and 😒?
faqs.a: 🙄 dismisses; 😒 resents. The eye roll treats something as silly or tedious. The unamused side-eye shows the sender is personally put out. They are often used together when someone is both annoyed and scornful.

faqs.q: When was the eye roll emoji added?
faqs.a: 🙄 was approved in 2015 in the same release as 🤔, 🤗, 🤐 and 🤑. Before it existed, people relied on 😒 or typed out “eye roll” and “smh.”
